title: A dictionary for your own texts
description: Save meanings and examples, then try the new words in sentences of your own.

blocks.text: A word from an email or a book asks to be understood more precisely: the shade of meaning, whether it fits, where it comes from. An elegant explanation sparks interest, but a long example can make the reading harder still.

quote.text: So easily being able to trace the roots of words feels like ancient secrets are being whispered to me. Words are truly alive and they sing their truth through their origins.

blocks.text: First comes the meaning in the original phrase and a short example. Further meanings and the etymology are available alongside. The person saves the context and tries a sentence of their own; at review they see which question brought them to the word.
Test it on a sentence of your own

This one scenario doesn’t by itself justify a big new dictionary. You could start with personal notes layered over good reference material. The quality of the examples and explanations matters more than a daily stream of random words.
